learning: If the oval holds at 20/20 and bend progress rises above 0.17 and 0.12, lead is a useful lever. If the oval drops, shorter lead also hurts, and the bend limit is likely footprint or spread.
notes: Baseline controller kept unchanged so the y=0.03 sensor lead is the only variable. Lead moved back from y=0.05 because forward lead (y=0.07) collapsed the oval in iteration 3.
rationale: The evidence so far favours the iteration-0 baseline. It is the only design that finishes the oval (20/20, 1.65 s, oscillation 0.15). Moving the sensors forward to y=0.07 (iteration 3) collapsed the oval to 0/20 off-track at progress 0.16 and barely moved the bends (s-bend 0.21, slalom 0.12), so forward lead is the wrong direction. The Builder's proposal now moves the sensors back to y=0.03 with everything else at baseline. I have no race evidence for y=0.03 itself, so I keep the controller identical to the baseline (kp 2.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.8, weights [2,1,0,-1,-2], last_direction). That keeps the geometry change as the only variable and avoids confounding the lead test with a controller change. Reduced lead means the signal reacts later, so I do not add gain that could overshoot; the oval's 1.65 s finish leaves time margin at 1.8 base_speed. Sensor x positions, pitch and footprint are unchanged from the proposal. Expected result is an oval finish rate at or near 20/20 with oscillation at or below 0.15. Bend progress is uncertain: lead may help or hurt, and I cannot yet tell which.
